legend.critical: Blocks revenue or compliance. Needs your action before the platform can operate.
legend.high: Materially limits a feature or the dataset. Workaround documented.
legend.medium: Informational / expected behaviour, recorded for completeness.

rows.item: Product link 1 — `https://link.amazon/B04G1MEwY`
rows.finding: The host `link.amazon` is live and served from Amazon infrastructure (resolves to 18.172.170.20/.59/.77/.98). The submitted path is the problem, not the domain: it did not select the intended product.
rows.action: Re-supply as `https://www.amazon.com/dp/<10-char ASIN>?tag=<your-associates-tag>` or a genuine `amzn.to` Smart Link generated in Associates Central.

rows.item: Product link 2 — `https://link.amazon/B02NbDxp3`
rows.finding: Same failure mode as FLG-001.
rows.action: Re-supply the exact 10-character ASIN.

rows.item: Product link 3 — `https://link.amazon/B00hJ57DV`
rows.finding: Same failure mode as FLG-001.
rows.action: Re-supply the exact 10-character ASIN.

rows.item: Identifier `B04G1MEwY`
rows.finding: 9 characters. Amazon states an ASIN is "a unique 10-character alphanumeric code". `https://www.amazon.com/dp/B04G1MEwY` returns the Amazon 'Page Not Found' error page.
rows.action: Provide the full 10-character ASIN. Likely one character was dropped when the link was copied.

rows.item: Identifier `B02NbDxp3`
rows.finding: 9 characters; same rule; /dp/ probe returns 'Page Not Found'.
rows.action: Provide the full 10-character ASIN.

rows.item: Identifier `B00hJ57DV`
rows.finding: 9 characters; same rule; /dp/ probe returns 'Page Not Found'.
rows.action: Provide the full 10-character ASIN. Note this one begins `B00`, the prefix pattern Amazon documents for older ASINs, so a dropped trailing character is plausible.

rows.item: Redirect targets differ per request — decisive evidence the IDs are meaningless
rows.finding: The three submitted links resolved to three DIFFERENT, unrelated products: B0CDY277D3 (CHEFMAN 6-Qt dual-basket air fryer), B09B7SB46R (Emeril Lagasse 26QT air fryer toaster oven) and B08DKYBTPH (Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt). Every final URL carries `channelId=704&plpRedirect=mhFallback` — Amazon's fallback route, not a product deep link.
rows.action: Do not treat any of those three landing pages as product data. They are Amazon's own recommendations, served at random. None of them is recorded anywhere in this dataset.

rows.item: 12 product attribute fields x 3 SKUs = 36 cells
rows.finding: Title, brand, category, price, used price, rating, review count, availability, variations, per-category commission, trend signal and competition density are all blank. No official source exists for any of them while the identifier is invalid.
rows.action: Valid ASIN + approved Creators API credentials. Until then these cells stay blank by design rather than being estimated.

rows.item: Scraping was rejected as a data source
rows.finding: Product, price, rating and review data may only be obtained via Creators API / PA API or a link Amazon serves; storing images is prohibited and other Program Content may be cached for at most 24 hours. Automated scraping of amazon.com to backfill these tables would breach the Program Policies, so it was not done.
rows.action: Use Creators API GetItems as the sole intake. No action needed from you — this is a guard-rail the platform enforces.

rows.item: Repository baseline
rows.finding: At branch creation `main` held exactly one commit, `ed1a796` "Initial commit", containing one file: `README.md`, 7 bytes, contents `# Zone3`. No prior code, data, CI, or `COORDINATION.md` existed to review.
rows.action: Nothing — recorded so the audit trail has a defined starting point.

rows.item: No Associates tag / account credential supplied
rows.finding: Affiliate link generation and attribution testing both require your own Associates ID in the form `XXXXX-##` plus approved API credentials. Neither was provided, and neither can be derived or guessed.
rows.action: Add `associates_tag` to `config/platform.json` (or set `ZONE3_ASSOCIATES_TAG`) and register for Creators API in Associates Central.

rows.item: Click and conversion tracking
rows.finding: Amazon, not the associate, is the system of record: it "will use commercially reasonable efforts to accurately and comprehensively track Qualifying Purchases" and pays ~60 days after month end. There is no public endpoint to pull those numbers, so the ledger ships empty and instrumented.
rows.action: Export Earnings Reports from Associates Central monthly and ingest them into `data/campaign-metrics.json`; or leave the manual-entry form for it.

rows.item: Per-category commission rates — CORRECTED after further verification
rows.finding: An earlier draft recorded these as unavailable because /help/operating/schedule redirects to sign-in. That was wrong: the Standard Commission Income Statement (Table 1) is published publicly at the Associates help centre, as is the Onsite statement. All 11 rate bands plus the Bounty rates are now on the Commission page with those citations.
rows.action: Resolved for category rates. What remains blank is only the per-product commission for P-01/P-02/P-03, because their category is unresolved while the identifiers are invalid — a category cannot be assigned to an unresolvable listing.

rows.item: PA-API 5.0 is deprecated — any existing integration is dead
rows.finding: The PA-API 5.0 documentation host now returns a deprecation notice: PA-API 5 "has been deprecated and is being replaced by the Creators API", and live callers receive HTTP 403 Forbidden / `com.amazon.paapi5#AccessDeniedException`. Most third-party "Amazon affiliate AI" tooling in this space still documents PA-API 5 as current.
rows.action: Architect against Creators API only. Treat any vendor tutorial built on PA-API 5 as out of date.

rows.item: Link-shortener conflict with the submitted format
rows.finding: The submitted `link.amazon/...` shape is a short, opaque path link. Program rules prohibit using a link shortening service in a way that makes it unclear you are linking to Amazon, prohibit obscuring the destination URL, and disqualify purchases arriving via a Redirecting Link. `amzn.to` (the shortener most affiliates use) resolves to 67.199.248.12/.13 — a third-party shortener range, not an Amazon address block.
rows.action: Use full, self-assembled `amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=<your-tag>` links for content you generate. Reserve Smart Links for channels where Amazon supplies the link directly.

rows.item: "Trending" and "high-converting" product detection
rows.finding: The brief asks the agent to identify trending and high-converting products and analyse competition. No official Amazon API provides trend rank, competitor density or conversion rate to affiliates: Creators API exposes only SearchItems, GetItems, GetVariations and GetBrowseNodes. Amazon also publishes no conversion-rate figure for affiliates. Any tool claiming these numbers derives them from scraping or a model, not from Amazon.
rows.action: Either accept a proxy method you explicitly approve (e.g. SearchItems result count + publish date + rating count as an estimate, clearly labelled as an estimate) or drop these columns. No proxy values were computed here, because none could be sourced.

rows.item: "Track clicks and continuously optimize campaigns" vs. the sub-tag rule
rows.finding: Per-user click tracking by dynamic sub-tagging is forbidden: "Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users' behavior)."
rows.action: Campaign optimisation must be page-level or slot-level with STATIC sub-tags only. The platform's optimiser is designed to that limit; no per-visitor attribution is attempted.

rows.item: "Analyze pricing" vs. the price-alerting ban
rows.finding: "Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality." A price-drop alert or a tracked-price history on the site is therefore not permitted, even though analysing price data internally is.
rows.action: Pricing analysis is kept internal (ranking, threshold for 'deal' claims) and the site only ever displays a point-in-time price with the required timestamp and disclaimer. No alerts, no price history charts.

rows.item: Agents must self-declare in the User-Agent
rows.finding: New Agent Terms (IP License SS4) define an "Agent" as "any software or service that takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action on behalf of, or at the instruction of, any person or entity", and require every HTTP/HTTPS request to identify itself with `Agent/[agent name]` in the User-Agent string. Agents must not mimic human interaction patterns, must not complete CAPTCHAs, must answer truthfully when asked whether they are human, and must not circumvent access controls.
rows.action: Set `User-Agent: ... Agent/Zone3ProductResearch` on every outbound request this platform makes. Already wired into `tools/amazon_intake.py`.

rows.item: Creators API access is gated behind a sales threshold
rows.finding: Prerequisite as published: "Have at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days to access the PA API through the Creators API". A brand-new account therefore cannot use the API at all.
rows.action: Bootstrap with 10 qualifying sales using non-API links (SiteStripe-generated Smart Links) before the automated research loop can run. The platform is built to queue research jobs until credentials are present.

rows.item: "Publish and manage affiliate links" — where publishing is NOT allowed
rows.finding: Special Links may not be placed in any content on an Amazon Site (customer reviews, forums, Wish Lists, guides), may not be posted on Amazon itself, may not appear in pop-ups/pop-unders or transitional ads, and must not be encouraged to be bookmarked. Buying paid search on keywords containing "amazon"/"kindle" or any Amazon Mark disqualifies the resulting purchase entirely.
rows.action: The publishing module targets owned properties (this site, your blog, your newsletter) only. Automated posting to Amazon or to paid Amazon-brand keywords is disabled in the design.

rows.item: Paid "Amazon affiliate automation" services are unauthorised
rows.finding: Amazon states the Associates Program is free to join and: "We have never authorized any business to provide paid set-up or consulting services to our associates, so please be wary if any business like that (even one attempting to appropriate the Amazon name) reaches out to offer you costly services."
rows.action: Relevant if you evaluate third-party 'done-for-you Amazon AI' vendors. This platform is self-hosted in your repo and asks for no payment to any intermediary.

rows.item: AI-generated content and review integrity
rows.finding: The Operating Agreement incorporates Amazon's Community Guidelines "including the prohibition of customer reviews that are created, edited, or removed in exchange for compensation". An LLM on this platform generates editorial articles only; it must never be pointed at generating Amazon customer reviews, and the site must not present AI-written praise as an independent review.
rows.action: Kept as an explicit design boundary. Editorial pages carry the Amazon text disclaimer and the associate disclosure; no synthetic reviews exist or are generated.

rows.item: Programme termination risk if anything here is automated badly
rows.finding: Violation of Section 5 (identification/disclosure) is deemed a material breach, and Amazon reserves the right to "permanently cease payment of ... any and all commission income" for violations. Accounts can also be closed for sites that are unsuitable or that lack original content; the agreement is terminable by either party on 7 calendar days' notice.
rows.action: Treat the disclosure + original-content requirements as release gates, not copy. `tools/verify_site.py` fails the build if a page is missing the disclosure block.

rows.item: Inherited page shipped without the required Associates disclosure
rows.finding: Cross-session finding from integration. category/kitchen.html — authored by an earlier session and NOT produced by scripts/build_site.py — had no Associates disclosure anywhere on the page, while every page their generator emits does carry it (DISCLOSURE is defined at scripts/build_site.py line 24). So the gap was in a hand-authored file, which no generator-level check would ever catch. Operating Agreement SS5 requires the sentence wherever Program Content is displayed, and SS6 deems its omission a material breach, so this was not left as a note on a board.
rows.action: Fixed additively during integration: the disclosure bar was inserted into the shipped page, plus a sentence clarifying that the 4.50 % Kitchen figure is a category reference and not attributed to any product whose category is unverified. No other session content was altered. Recommend their check_site.py audit every *.html under the root rather than only generated pages — this site's verify_site.py already walks the whole tree, which is how the gap was found.

rows.item: Two site generations now coexist at the repository root
rows.finding: main carries an earlier flat-page site (index/products/pricing/reviews/content/campaigns/sources/flagged .html, built by scripts/build_site.py from data/*.json). This session renders 16 directory-style pages from data/z3/*.json via tools/build_site.py. The root landing page is now this session's build; the previous landing page is preserved verbatim at landing-prior.html, and this session's JS moved to assets/dashboard.js so assets/app.js stays owned by its original author.
rows.action: Decide one canonical generator and migrate, or keep both with the root pointing at one. Deliberately NOT resolved by deletion: removing another session's pages would destroy data that the shared board says belongs to them. Nothing here needs your input to stay live — both page sets are served and both pass their own checks.

rows.item: Two sessions resolved the same three links differently
rows.finding: Session 3c886b62 (published under `sessions/3c886b62/`) treats the target of each `link.amazon` redirect as the submitted product: it records ASIN B0CDY277D3 for `B04G1MEwY` with status `verified` and derives title, brand and department from that page. This build treats the submission as unresolved and leaves every dependent cell blank. Both readings rest on the same observations — the submitted code is 9 characters, `/dp/<code>` returns Page Not Found, and the short link lands on another product through `plpRedirect=mhFallback`. The divergence is one sentence of interpretation: whether Amazon's fallback target *is* the product. Three different submitted codes produced three different targets, which is the evidence this build relied on to answer no.
rows.action: Not resolvable from public documents; it needs the original submission context. Ask whoever supplied the links for the ten characters, or for the pages they were copied from. Until then the two tables should not be presented as interchangeable, and this site does not merge their product values into its own rows.

rows.item: Published prices and ratings need the IP License timestamp treatment
rows.finding: `sessions/3c886b62/data/products.json` displays prices ($79.93, $149.99, $79.91) and star ratings (4.2, 4.3, 4.4) marked `verified`, read from Amazon search-results renderings. That session's own register already flags the display rules around this (F01 for Part. Req. 2(b), F02 for 5(t), F16 for point-in-time capture), so the exposure is documented rather than unnoticed. Two mechanical gaps remain for the published pages: IP License 2(i) requires prices not refreshed hourly to carry an adjacent date/time stamp plus the verbatim price-and-availability sentence, and 5(t) admits ratings only when obtained through Creators/PA API — a value read off a rendered page does not qualify even though the number is correct on the day it was read.
rows.action: Two ways to close it, both cheap: put the timestamp and the verbatim 2(i) disclaimer next to each price on the page, and label the rating cells as page-rendered rather than API-sourced; or move both into a table titled as an observation of the fallback page with the date it was read. Do not relabel them as API data — that is the one change that would turn a dated observation into a false claim.
